notes: A plain unit's line is a frame plus, outside the dry tone, one of the unit's own lines for that tone. Frames say what the figure is; lines are the punchline and never carry a count.
singles are for a figure between one and two of a unit, where a multiplier would read as noise.
Tone keys: dry | nerd | roast. The user picks one or a mix in Settings.
discrete: true means the unit is a countable object; the multiplier is floored to a whole number.
Token values are NOT stored. Units declare 'words', 'codeLines' or 'tokens'; the engine multiplies by conversions at load.
confidence: verified = natively denominated in the metric it claims. approx = derived through an assumed ratio. volatile = changes over time.

kind: unit = plain ratio. derived = formula over the input alone. composite = formula plus a reference unit the engine picks, gated on 'requires'. Derived and composite units carry 'templates', a list of sentences per tone.
Keep a finished line under about 130 characters so it fits the dashboard on two lines.

Frame slots: {label} is the unit as a noun phrase with its article ('the King James Bible'); {many} is its plural for counting ('copies of Dune', never 'Dunes'); {count} and {times} are the multiplier in words ('eight and a half', 'nearly nine times', 'twice', 'about 1,200 times'). A frame using {many} or {count} is used only for units that declare 'many'.

{lead} and {tail} place the period a figure covers: 'Today alone, ' at the start, ' today' inside the sentence. Both are empty when no period is given. With a period, only frames that carry one of them are used, so every line says which period it means.
facts: the dry tone's aside, built from a unit's own quantity so it can never disagree with the figure the comparison used.

conversions.note: Claude Code's 'Dune' comparison implies words x ~1.3. Code averages ~9 tokens/line for C-family source. Both are English/Latin-script assumptions; adjust if you ever localise.

tokens: Stack up {count} {many} and you're about there.
